extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (researchers/engineers using the rstandard.lib library)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for the SINGULAR library procedure modBorder: how to call it, what it returns, and a worked example showing loading the library, setting a ring, building an ideal, and invoking modBorder to compute a (modular) border basis. Emphasis on the verification flag for the second argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure source / cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from library rstandard.lib (see Section D.15.33 [rstandard lib], page 2215).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates modBorder is implemented in rstandard.lib and points to the library section for further context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage (function signature)
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage:

modBorder(I,i); I is an ideal, i an integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call with the first argument I being the ideal whose border basis is desired and the second an integer flag controlling verification (see verification flag entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Return value
rubrics_metrics.description:
Return:

ideal, a border basis for I using modular methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure returns an ideal that represents a border basis computed via modular techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification flag behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: If second argument is 0 then the result is not verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a nonzero second argument (e.g., 1) to request verification of the computed border basis; using 0 yields an unverified result (faster but unverified).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Computes a border basis for the ideal given by the generators in I using modular techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use modBorder when a border basis (via modular methods) is needed for an ideal specified by its generators. The routine is intended to produce a border basis representation of the input ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical usage workflow (example)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrates the typical steps: load the library, set the ring, define a polynomial f, form an ideal (here using jacob(f) and adding f), then call modBorder with verification (1) and print the resulting ideal j. Use analogous steps for other inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example outputs / expected form
rubrics_metrics.description: The example shows the returned ideal elements printed as j[1]=..., j[2]=..., etc. (concrete polynomials and relations compose the border basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect the printed j[...] list to see the computed border basis generators; they may include polynomial combinations and rational coefficients produced by the modular computations.
